rule: Exact own selected Infobox Item bankable=No, or the separately bound two direct no-deposit blasters, excludes ordinary unobserved bank-deposit candidates. Bank notes deposit as their converted state; identity edges never grant raw-state semantics. Preserve every valid observed bank row including zero-quantity placeholders and legacy/exploit copies. Missing, tradeability, noteability, cannot-leave, acquisition or mode alone is not no-bank proof.
rootSemanticDecision: Approve the 719 exact direct prohibitions after reconciling 718 audited strict cases plus two own-prose blasters. Quarantine Cyan crystal: its bank failure is explicitly post-quest and pre-quest scope is not proved. Hold Canopic quest-phase storage, Jim legacy retained rows and Bulging taxbag exploit-created bank rows. Nonbank-container or GE persistence is not a bank deposit permission; never erase an actually observed row.
tagsAndSecondaryRoles: unassessed; no category or tag claims from this deposit policy

cases.name: Bronze axe head
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bronze axe head detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''bronze axe head''' is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while [[Woodcutting]]. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the [[Axe handle (historical)|axe handle]].

A similar event used to happen to players while [[Mining]], but with a [[pickaxe head]] and [[pickaxe handle]].

Axe heads were removed in an update on 17 July 2007, prior to the release of Old School RuneScape, so have never been obtainable.

cases.name: Orb of light
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Orb of light detail.png|left|160px]]
An '''orb of light''', also known as a '''Sphere of Light''', is a magical orb used in [[Underground Pass]] [[quest]]. The player destroys four of these orbs in the [[furnace]] found in the dungeon in order to progress into the next part (note: one cannot destroy the orbs in another furnace outside the underground pass). Destroying an orb yields the message, ''You feel a cold shudder run down your spine as the light of the orb fades.''

According to the [[old journal]], they were placed in the [[Underground Pass (dungeon)|Underground Pass]] by the warrior, [[Randas]], in a failed attempt to ward off the darkness prior to the player's involvement.

Orbs of light cannot be banked, and duplicates cannot be held or picked up after that version is destroyed (spawn version or player-dropped version). The item spawn cannot be seen by [[Telekinetic Grab]], however, a player-dropped variant can, but the spell cannot be used on it.

cases.name: Rock-climbing boots
Lamp
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Lamp detail.png|left|200px]]
The '''lamp''' is a reward obtained from several [[random event]]s or by opening an [[Intricate pouch|Intricate Pouch]] that differs from those awarded by quests. While these lamps cannot be traded or banked, rubbing one gives the option of adding [[experience]] to any skill a player chooses. The amount given is ten times their skill level of choice (e.g. a skill at level 21 would give 210 experience).

Lamps always go to your gravestone on death unless protected.

cases.name: Bloated toad
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bloated toad detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Bloated toads''' are used to catch [[chompy bird]]s during and after the [[Big Chompy Bird Hunting]] [[quest]]. Their dyed variant, [[coloured toads]], are used during [[Mourning's End Part I]]. Bloated toads can be obtained by using [[ogre bellows]] which have been filled with swamp gas on a [[swamp toad]]. Only three toads may be obtained at one time, and they cannot be [[bank]]ed.

Bloated toads may only be dropped in the ogre areas east and south of [[Gu'Tanoth]]. Once dropped, they have a chance of causing a chompy bird to land, lasting 1 minute before exploding and dealing 1-2 damage to all players within one tile (including diagonally). This damage cannot kill players.

Inflating a toad a second time by using filled ogre bellows on a bloated toad will lead to the toad floating away in a comical manner if the player is not in the possession of a [[ball of wool]] and a [[Rock (elemental)|suitable rock]]; if these materials are available, however, a [[balloon toad]] will be created instead.

cases.name: Awful anthem
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Awful anthem detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''awful anthem''' is a [[quests|quest]] [[items|item]] used in the [[Throne of Miscellania]] quest. Players require a new anthem for Etceteria to replace the old one, which is the condition for the peace between [[Etceteria]] and [[Miscellania]].

Players can obtain one from the want-to-be bard [[Prince Brand]], the son of [[King Vargas]]. It is used to settle the war between Etceteria and Miscellania. The player must take the awful anthem to [[Advisor Ghrim]] who will then make a number of improvements to the song, turning it into a [[good anthem]], which must be taken to [[Queen Sigrid]]. The revised version of the anthem has a lighter colouring.

Attempting to bank the awful anthem prints the message {{mes|You have more urgent things to do with this anthem!}}. After the quest, players can no longer get the Awful anthem.

cases.name: Good anthem
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Good anthem detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''good anthem''' is a quest item used in the [[Throne of Miscellania]] quest. To obtain it the player must take the [[awful anthem]] to [[Advisor Ghrim]] who will then make a number of improvements to the song, turning it into a good anthem.

Attempting to bank the good anthem prints the message {{mes|You have more urgent things to do with this anthem!}}.

If lost, the player has to get another awful anthem from [[Prince Brand]] and give it to Advisor Ghrim.

Fire
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Fire (unobtainable item) detail.png|left|70px]]
'''Fire''' is an [[unobtainable item]] that was presumably intended for use during the [[Desert Treasure I]] quest. It would most likely have been found in the [[Smoke Dungeon]], as part of a subquest for finding the Fire diamond, alongside the fire key. As the fire diamond was changed to the [[smoke diamond]] instead, the fire key was changed to the [[Warm key]], and the Fire object was removed.

While on the ground it cannot be picked up. Instead, it has the option of "study", giving the message ''"A strangely bright burning flame..."''

cases.name: Cupric sulfate
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Cupric sulfate detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Cupric sulfate''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used only in [[Recruitment Drive]]. It is found in a bookcase in [[Miss Cheevers]]'s trial.

It is used on the stone door when the [[metal spade (head)|metal spade]] is inserted into the hole. A [[vial of liquid]] is used after to expand the spade in order to use it as a door handle. If combined incorrectly with other chemicals, it may result in a [[??? mixture]] or a [[tin (strange)|strange tin]].

After leaving the room, all copies in the inventory are deleted.

cases.name: Vial of liquid
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Vial of liquid detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''vial of liquid''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used only in [[Recruitment Drive]]. A set of three vials and an individual vial can be found in two separate bookcases in [[Miss Cheevers]]'s trial. According to the examine text, it is a vial of water.

It is used on the stone door when the [[metal spade (head)|metal spade]] is inserted into the hole after already used [[cupric sulfate]] on it to expand the spade to use it as a door handle. It is also used on the [[tin (gypsum)|gypsum tin]] to make a [[tin (hardening)|hardening tin]]. If combined incorrectly with other chemicals, it may result in [[??? mixture]] or a [[tin (strange)|strange tin]].

After leaving the room, all copies in the inventory are deleted.

cases.sourceContext:
{{Synced switch
|version1 = [[File:Metal spade detail.png|left|130px]]
|version2 = [[File:Metal spade (head) detail.png|left|130px]]
}}
The '''metal spade''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used only in [[Recruitment Drive]]. It is found on the table in [[Miss Cheevers]]'s trial.

It is used on a bunsen burner to remove the handle. The head is then put into a hole in the [[Open Door|door]]. Adding [[cupric sulfate]] and [[vial of liquid]] will heat the spade, expanding the metal and trapping it in the hole, at which point it can then be used as a handle to open the door.

Duplicates can be obtained after it has expanded, but it serves no further use. After leaving the room, all copies in the inventory are deleted.

cases.name: Alchemical notes
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Alchemical notes detail.png|left|140px]]
'''Alchemical notes''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used only in [[Recruitment Drive]]. It is found by searching an old bookshelf with a toy horse on it directly north of [[Miss Cheevers]] after asking her for help twice during her trial.

The notes describe various chemical reactions between items that the player can find during the [[quest]]. This information may be used in order to determine the correct reactions for the provided chemicals.

Duplicates can be [[drop trick]]ed by searching the old bookshelf to obtain another.

The '''??? mixture''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used only in [[Recruitment Drive]]. It is made by incorrectly mixing ingredients together during [[Miss Cheevers]]'s trial. There are three ??? mixtures obtainable during the quest, none of which are useful in completing the challenge. Because many of the ingredients cannot be retrieved after use, it is likely that the challenge must be restarted if a ??? mixture is created.

The hot mixture is made by using [[cupric sulfate]] on the [[vial of liquid]]. The warm mixture is made by using [[gypsum]] on a vial of liquid. The horrible mixture is made by adding cupric sulfate to anything else, or to another hot mixture.

cases.name: Hand mirror
Dragon axe head
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dragon axe head detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''dragon axe head''' is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while [[Woodcutting]]. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the [[Axe handle (historical)#Dragon|axe handle]].

As [[dragon axe]]s were worth over 2 million at the time, players who were not paying constant attention risked substantial losses. Curiously, although a special version of the Dragon axe handle was added in 2006, it was still possible to combine a Dragon axe head and a regular Axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while [[Mining]], but with a [[pickaxe head]] and [[pickaxe handle]].

Axe heads were removed in an update on 17 July 2007, prior to the release of Old School RuneScape, so have never been obtainable.

cases.name: Prison key
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Prison key (Prison Pete) detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''Prison key''' is part of the [[random event]] involving [[Prison Pete]]. It is obtained by popping one of the [[balloon animal]]s. Although it has a "return" option, the player automatically walks back to Prison Pete after he tells them to. If the correct balloon animal has been popped, this key will unlock one of the barriers. If not, another barrier will be added for you to unlock. Five barriers is the maximum amount. If the key is dropped it will vanish and the player must pop another balloon animal to get a new one.

In order to get the correct key, a player must pull the lever to find out which balloon animal they should pop. They should then pop the animal that looks exactly the same as the image you see after pulling the lever. This will ensure the key fits.

cases.sourceContext:
{{Synced switch

A '''balloon toad''' is a quest item used during [[Recipe for Disaster]], in the [[Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Skrach Uglogwee|Skrach Uglogwee]] subquest. It is the bait used when hunting for [[jubbly bird|jubblies]] in the [[Feldip Hills]]. It is made by using [[ogre bellows]] with swamp gas on a [[Swamp Toad|swamp toad]], receiving a [[bloated toad]]. Then, while having a [[ball of wool]] and [[rock (elemental)|rock]] in the inventory, the player must use the bellows on the toad again to create the balloon.

Once a player has set the trap, if the jubbly eats it or it blows away, the player loses the frog and rock but keeps hold of the wool. There are two additional options of ''Release'' and ''Release-all'' which may be used to set the frogs free. Although there is a drop option, it is used for setting the trap, and may only be used in some areas of the Feldip Hills. Therefore, the release option must be used for disposing of the item.

Using a [[rock (limestone)|limestone rock]] to make the balloon toad will give a balloon toad with a slightly different coloured rock, but they are functionally equivalent. After stringing 15 balloon toads, the wool is consumed and a message "Your ball of wool has been used up." is displayed in the game chat.

Attempting to bank this item will generate the message "A magical force prevents you from banking this item."

cases.name: Kettle
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Kettle detail.png|left|150px]]
A '''kettle''' is an item used to make a [[Cup of tea (Player-owned house)|cup of tea]] in the [[kitchen]] of a [[player-owned house]], allowing the player to temporarily boost [[Construction]] by up to 3 levels. An infinite number can be taken from any type of kitchen [[shelves|shelf]]. Players may use this item on a water source to produce a [[full kettle]]. If the player leaves the house this item will disappear from their inventory.

cases.name: Full kettle
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Full kettle detail.png|left|150px]]
A '''full kettle''' is an item used to make a [[Cup of tea (Player-owned house)|cup of tea]] in the [[kitchen]] of a [[player-owned house]], allowing the player to temporarily boost [[Construction]] by up to 3 levels. To make this item, players must use a [[kettle]] on a sink or other water source inside a player-owned house. Players can then use this item on a range to produce a [[hot kettle]]. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found [[Cup of tea (Player-owned house)#Making a cup of tea|here]].

'''Note:''' If a player leaves the house in any way, the item will disappear from their inventory.

{{Tea}}

cases.name: Hot kettle
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Hot kettle detail.png|left|150px]]
A '''hot kettle''' is an item used to make a [[Cup of tea (Player-owned house)|cup of tea]] in the [[kitchen]] of a [[player-owned house]] allowing the player to temporarily boost [[Construction]] by up to 3 levels. A player can obtain this item by placing a [[full kettle]] on a range and then removing the kettle from the range. Requiring level 20 [[Cooking]], players can use a hot kettle with a [[teapot with leaves]] in order to make a [[pot of tea]] and gain 52 experience. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found [[Cup of tea (Player-owned house)#Making a cup of tea|here]].

'''Note:''' If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.

cases.sourceContext:

Players can obtain this item by using a [[hot kettle]] with a [[teapot with leaves]]. When made, a pot of tea has four doses. Players must use the pot of tea on a [[Empty cup (clay)|clay cup]], [[Porcelain cup (porcelain)|porcelain cup]], or a [[Porcelain cup (trimmed)|trimmed porcelain cup]] producing a cup of tea to make the tea drinkable. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found [[Cup of tea (Player-owned house)#Making a cup of tea|here]].

'''Note:''' If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.

A pot of tea comes in three different colours depending on the shelf that the [[teapot]] was taken from. A clay teapot can be taken from [[Wooden shelves 1]] (6 Construction), [[Wooden shelves 2]] (12 Construction), and [[Oak shelves 1]] (34 Construction). Despite the different teapots, the boost only depends on the type of cup used.

cases.name: Moonlight mead
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Moonlight mead (player-owned house) detail.png|left|150x150px]]
'''Moonlight mead''' is an unobtainable item intended for use in [[Construction]]. It is a variant of [[moonlight mead]] that would have been obtained in a [[player-owned house]]. Players could have obtained it by using an [[Beer glass (Player-owned house)|empty beer glass]] on a moonlight mead barrel.

For unknown reasons, the Moonlight mead barrel was never added to the game, so the item it produces is unobtainable.

cases.name: Dark essence fragments
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dark essence fragments detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Dark essence fragments''' are items created by using a [[chisel]] on [[dark essence block]]s, providing 8 [[Crafting]] experience per block. Each block will create 4 pieces of essence, which are used to [[runecraft]] [[blood rune|blood]] and [[soul rune]]s. Players cannot hold more than 108 fragments at a time, with 111 at a maximum if a stack of 108 is picked up while holding a stack of 4+. The fragments cannot be stored in a bank. Dark essence fragments vanish upon [[death]].

*[[Blood runes]] can be made at [[Blood Altar (Kourend)|Kourend's Blood Altar]] at 77 Runecraft (can be boosted) and will provide 23.8 experience per dark essence fragment.

*[[Soul runes]] can be made at 90 Runecraft and will provide 29.7 experience per dark essence fragment.

cases.name: Pipe section
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Pipe section detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''pipe section''' is an item used in the [[Trouble Brewing]] minigame to repair sabotaged [[Bamboo Pipes|bamboo pipes]] and [[Water Pump (Trouble Brewing)|water pumps]]. At the start of each game, 10 pipe sections are stocked in the [[workbench (Trouble Brewing, tools)|tool workbench]], and crafted pipe sections can be used on the workbench to store them within it. 

Pipe sections can be crafted by using a regular [[log]] on the [[Workbench (Trouble Brewing)|large workbench]]. [[Log]]s can be gathered from the [[log store]] within your team's base, or by chopping down the various [[tree]]s around your base with an [[axe]]. [[Scrapey tree logs]] cannot be crafted into pipe sections. Creating a pipe section rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair something rewards the same amount.

cases.name: Lumber patch
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Lumber patch detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''lumber patch''' is used in the [[Trouble Brewing]] minigame to repair [[Hopper (Trouble Brewing)|hoppers]] which have been burnt by other players. It can take up to three patches to repair a hopper, depending on how long it was on fire for. At the start of each game, 10 lumber patches are stocked in the [[workbench (Trouble Brewing, tools)|tool workbench]], and crafted lumber patches can be used on the workbench to store them within it. 

Lumber patches can be crafted by using a regular [[log]] on the [[Workbench (Trouble Brewing)|large workbench]]. [[Log]]s can be gathered from the [[log store]] within your team's base, or by chopping down the various [[tree]]s around your base with an [[axe]]. [[Scrapey tree logs]] cannot be crafted into lumber patches. Creating a lumber patch rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair a hopper rewards the same amount.

cases.name: Scrapey tree logs
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Scrapey tree logs detail.png|left|140px]]
'''Scrapey tree logs''' are items used in the [[Trouble Brewing]] [[minigame]]. They can be obtained by chopping the [[scrapey tree]]s found within the brewing area. To use the logs to produce rum, players must use a [[knife]] on them, which will yield [[scrapey bark]]. Doing so has a 1/50 chance to cause the player to become [[disease]]d.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1478180485411004425|date=3 January 2022|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/109848|archivedate=4 January 2022|quote=No, that's 1/50 flat rate.}}

A '''bowl of red water''' is an item obtained within the [[minigame]] [[Trouble Brewing]]. It is made by using a [[bowl]] on the kettle with [[Red flowers (Trouble Brewing)|red flowers]] in it. It is an ingredient to make [[rum (red)|rum]] and can be put in the hopper; doing so will result in gaining 100 Cooking experience. It is an ingredient to make [[rum (blue)|rum]] and can be put in the hopper; doing so will result in gaining 100 Cooking experience. cases.name: Bitternut
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bitternut detail.png|left|100px]]
'''Bitternuts''' are items used in the [[Trouble Brewing]] minigame. Players can obtain the nuts from the bitternut trees found within the minigame on [[Mos Le'Harmless]] using [[Monkey (Trouble Brewing)|monkeys]], which are caught in the same area. 

In order to retrieve a bitternut, the player must first dye a monkey in the colour of their team using [[Bowl of red water|red water]] or [[Bowl of blue water|blue water]], obtained by using either [[Red flowers (Trouble Brewing)|red]] or [[Blue flowers (Trouble Brewing)|blue flowers]] on the kettle in your team's base and then using an empty bowl on the kettle. They then can use the [[Monkey (Trouble Brewing)|monkey]] with the [[Bitternut Tree]]. 

Additionally, if you have a [[Monkeyspeak amulet]] or have completed [[Monkey Madness II]], you can alter the strategy used. You can choose to either make the monkey angry by taunting it, or caution him. By making him angry, he'll be more inclined to get up the tree as fast as possible and start pelting you with bitternuts, speeding up the time before you get a nut. If you tell him to be careful, he'll take a little bit longer, but will be more aware of other monkeys and will be more likely to win in a confrontation. This is also the most complicated task in [[Trouble Brewing]].

Players may only have 2 bitternuts in their inventory at one time. If the player attempts to gather more while having two in their inventory already, the monkey will return home without giving the player another bitternut. When obtained players are granted 50 [[Hunter]] experience. Bitternuts can be used on the team's hopper, gaining 200 [[Cooking]] experience in the process.

According to [[Varrock Museum]], monkeys on both [[Karamja]] and [[Mos Le'Harmless]] are very fond of bitternuts, although the nuts can only be found by players on [[Mos Le'Harmless]].

cases.name: Scrapey bark
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Scrapey bark detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Scrapey bark''' is used in the [[Trouble Brewing]] [[minigame]]. Players may obtain bark by using a [[knife]] with the [[scrapey tree logs]] obtained from chopping [[scrapey tree]]s, granting 50 [[Fletching]] experience. Doing so has a 1/50 chance to cause the player to become [[disease]]d.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1478180485411004425|date=3 January 2022|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/109848|archivedate=4 January 2022|quote=No, that's 1/50 flat rate.}} They must then be placed in their corresponding factory hopper, and doing so will provide the player with 100 [[Cooking]] experience.

cases.name: Bridge section
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bridge section detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''bridge section''' is an item used in the [[Trouble Brewing]] minigame that will repair [[Bridge (Trouble Brewing)|bridges]] damaged by fires.  It can take up to three bridge sections to repair a bridge, depending on how long it was on fire for. At the start of each game, 10 bridge sections are stocked in the [[workbench (Trouble Brewing, tools)|tool workbench]], and crafted bridge sections can be used on the workbench to store them within it. 

Bridge sections can be crafted by using a regular [[log]] on the [[Workbench (Trouble Brewing)|large workbench]]. [[Log]]s can be gathered from the [[log store]] within your team's base, or by chopping down the various [[tree]]s around your base with an [[axe]]. [[Scrapey tree logs]] cannot be crafted into bridge sections. Creating a bridge section rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair a bridge rewards the same amount.

cases.name: Sweetgrubs
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Sweetgrubs detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Sweetgrubs''' are insects used during [[Trouble Brewing]], and are a key ingredient in the brewing of [[Rum (Trouble Brewing)|rum]] within the [[minigame]], serving as a substitute to the [[sluglings]] that [[Braindeath 'rum']] uses. They have a "gag-inducing" aftertaste, but are otherwise quite sweet, hence the name.{{CiteNPC|npc=San Fan|quote=Well, lacking any sluglings in the area, we add these little grubs called Sweetgrubs. If you ignore the gag- inducing aftertaste, they are quite sweet.|loc=|notes=|name=}} Sweetgrubs live in large [[Sweetgrub Mound]]s found on both sides of the Trouble Brewing facility.

[[Raw rat meat]] can be used on the mounds to collect sweetgrubs, with 40 [[Hunter]] experience being awarded for each sweetgrub successfully collected. When attempting to draw out some sweetgrubs from a mound, there is a 1/5 chance that the mound will empty out and collapse.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1263417999991726080|date=21 May 2020|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/102549|archivedate=2 February 2023|quote=1/5 for it depleting. If that doesn't happen, there's a separate 1/5 roll for getting flies.}} Players will have to find another mound or wait for it to fill again.  

If the mound does not collapse after the player uses their meat on it, there is a further 1/5 chance that a swarm of [[sweetflies]] will be drawn out instead. The sweetflies will continue to attack the player until they run away, as they cannot be attacked in retaliation. No one can gather more sweetgrubs from the mound while there are still sweetflies present.

The '''tome of experience''' is received from [[Veliaf Hurtz]] on completion of the [[Darkness of Hallowvale]] [[quest]]. Reading it opens a window to select the [[skill]] a player wishes to advance. The player must be at least level 30 in their chosen skill.

It has three chapters which provide 2000 experience each. After confirming, the player receives the message "''You read a fascinating chapter and earn experience! You have been awarded 2,000 (skill) experience!''" After the third reading, the book disappears and the player receives the message "''The book crumbles into a dust cloud of knowledge.''"

This item cannot be banked.

If lost or destroyed, the tome can be reclaimed by talking to [[Veliaf Hurtz]] in the [[Myreque Hideout]] under [[Burgh de Rott]], or from the chest in the same hideout after completing [[A Taste of Hope]].

'''No eggs''' is an unobtainable item released along with [[Barbarian Assault]], used on the Barbarian Assault in-game interface to represent that no eggs of a particular colour have been deposited.

[[Category:Interface items]]

cases.name: Documents
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Documents detail.png|150px|left]]
The '''Documents''' are an [[unobtainable item]] added to the cache alongside [[The Fremennik Isles]]. They have an option to "Open", while their examine states they must be taken to [[Ali Morrisane]] in [[Al Kharid]].

The documents' internal name suggest they formed part of a trade agreement, while the [[Royal decree]] is referred to as a "receipt", despite not serving this purpose. At the same time, many unused models can be found depicting crates of armour, swords, and battleaxes. It is possible therefore that there was a cut subplot in the quest which involved trading [[Jatizso]] products with Ali Morrisane.

Empty tax bag
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Empty tax bag detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''empty tax bag''' is used during [[The Fremennik Isles]] [[quest]] for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of [[Jatizso]]. While collecting taxes, it will become a [[light tax bag]], then a [[normal tax bag]], and finally a [[hefty tax bag]]. Tax bags cannot be banked, as "a magical force prevents you from banking this item!"

Selecting the Destroy option for a broken Power box immediately removes it from the game without a warning.

When bringing the broken part to [[Turgall]], he says ''"Oh, look at that broken part. Let me take it off you."''

Teleporting out of the agility course with the item will also cause it to break.

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Chocolate chunks (2013 Easter event) detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Chocolate chunks''' were used in the [[2013 Easter event]]. They could be obtained by smashing [[chocolate kebbit]]s and were given to the [[Easter Bunny]] for part of the reward. To smash them, the player used the Easter [[egg]]s on it by bowling them.

They are [[tradeable|non-tradeable]] and may not be banked - if a player attempts to deposit some in a [[bank]], the message ''"A magical force prevents you from banking this item!"'' appears in the [[chat|chat window]].

After the event ended, all chocolate chunks turned into [[chocolate dust]].

cases.name: Antique lamp
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Antique lamp (Karamja Diary) detail.png|left|180px]]
The '''antique lamp''' is an item obtained from completing the easy, medium, or hard tasks of the [[Karamja Diary]]. Unlike the other diaries, the antique lamps from the aforementioned tasks of the diary give different experience:
* The easy lamp grants 1,000 [[experience]] in a [[skill]] of the player's choosing with no level requirement.
* The medium lamp grants 5,000 [[experience]] in a [[skill]] of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 30.
* The hard lamp grants 10,000 [[experience]] in a [[skill]] of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 40.

Completing the elite Karamja diary gives the regular [[Antique lamp (elite)|elite Antique lamp]].

cases.name: Book of Knowledge
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Book of Knowledge detail.png|left|140px]]
A '''book of knowledge''' is the reward from [[Surprise Exam]] [[random events]]. Reading it grants [[experience]] equivalent to 15 times the level of the selected [[skills|skill]], 50% more than a [[Lamp|genie lamp]]'s 10 times multiplier. Two books of knowledge '''cannot''' be obtained at once, however it is still possible to get a second Surprise Exam random event. The player will receive an item instead. Possible rewards include an [[uncut gem]], [[loop half of key]], [[cosmic talisman]], or [[coins]]. 

If no inventory space is available, the book will be put on floor, but once picked up it cannot be dropped. Attempting to bank a book of knowledge yields the message: ''"A magical force prevents you from banking this item!"''.

The book is lost upon death.

[[File:Experience reward interface.png|thumb|left|The interface when using the book.]]

cases.name: Raw pheasant
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Raw pheasant detail.png|100px|left]]
A '''raw pheasant''' is obtained by killing a [[pheasant]] in the [[Freaky Forester]] [[random event]]. A raw pheasant must be given to the Freaky Forester to complete the event. The meat from any pheasant can be given to the Freaky Forester despite him asking for the meat of a specific bird.

Raw pheasants disappear if dropped. Attempting to attack another pheasant with one in the inventory results in the message {{mes|You already have a pheasant carcass. You don't need to kill another.}} If the player kills two pheasants (so there are two carcasses on the ground) and picks one up, attempting to pick up the second one results in the message {{mes|You already have a pheasant carcass in your inventory, you don't need to kill another.}} After handing in a raw pheasant and being told to leave, attempting to attack a pheasant results in the message {{mes|You don't need to attack any more pheasants. You're allowed to leave.}} A second raw pheasant can be picked up after giving the first one to the Freaky Forester, but it is removed from the inventory when leaving the event area.

cases.name: Anti-dragon shield (nz)
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Anti-dragon shield (nz) detail.png|left|150px]]
An '''anti-dragon shield (nz)''' is a [[Nightmare Zone]] exclusive version of an [[anti-dragon shield]], and shares its combat stats. It spawns on the ground if [[Elvarg]] is present in a Nightmare Zone session, as protection against her [[dragonfire]] attack.

As with all items with the (nz) suffix, it cannot be taken outside of the Nightmare Zone, and if discarded, can be retrieved from the same place it spawned.

cases.name: Pay-dirt
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Pay-dirt detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Pay-dirt''' is obtained while mining [[ore vein]]s within the [[Motherlode Mine]]. Mining pay-dirt grants 60 (up to 61.5 with full [[prospector outfit]]) [[Mining]] experience and requires a minimum Mining level of 30. Pay-dirt can be cleaned by depositing them into the [[hopper (Motherlode Mine)|hopper]] in the centre of the mine. Once cleaned players must search a [[Sack (Motherlode Mine)|sack]] to claim their ores, which is dependent on the player's Mining level. Pay-dirt cannot be deposited in the bank.

Players have a 1/32 (~3.13%) chance of obtaining a [[golden nugget]] per pay-dirt, which can be used to purchase the [[prospector outfit]] and other mining-related rewards from [[Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop]]. The number of golden nuggets received is limited to 3 per batch of pay-dirt deposited into the hopper. While this limit doesn't cause issues during normal gameplay, seasonal events with boosted rates can cause golden nuggets to be deleted. To avoid this, players can deposit half of their pay-dirt at a time by dropping the other half before depositing.

Which ore the pay-dirt becomes is determined at the time it is mined. If using a temporary boost, to try to get ore above your level, use the boost '''while mining''', as opposed to using the boost at the hopper and sack.

The double-ore bonus from [[Varrock armour]] does not apply to pay-dirt.

|desc = The sound effect played when mining pay-dirt.
}}

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Easter blaster detail.png|left|130px]]
[[File:Easter blaster.gif|frame|A player using the Easter blaster.]]
The '''Easter blaster''' is obtained during the [[2015 Easter event]]. It is made by using an [[empty blaster]] on several [[volatile mineral]]s, then using it on some oily substances near the mining site in the Easter Bunny's warren.

The Easter blaster cannot be used in combat in any way outside of the warren area meaning it becomes a cosmetic item after completing the Easter Event. This item cannot be banked as "a magical force prevents you from banking this item".

cases.name: Bank key
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bank key detail.png|100px|left]]
The '''bank key''' is a [[Deadman Mode]] item that allows 10 of the victim's most valuable items, based on [[Grand Exchange]] value, to be taken. It can be obtained by killing a player. The player that obtained the key can collect the items by opening a chest in a bank within a low-threat area, which means they must wait until their skull expires or risk being killed by the guards. These bank keys cannot be deposited into a bank, and only five bank keys can be in a player's possession at any given time.

Players who attempt to destroy a bank key must wait for a 10 second countdown displayed in the chatbox, similar when attempting to teleport or log out. Players may cast [[High Level Alchemy]] or [[Low Level Alchemy]] on it to receive 0gp.

[[File:Deadman chest.png|thumb|left|200px|A deadman chest, which requires a bank key to open.]]
If a player kills a player who is in possession of another bank key, they will drop their own bank key in addition to their victim's bank keys. If a skulled player dies to a guard, 10 of their most valuable items from the bank are dropped wherever they die. Additionally, the player will lose 10% of all of their protected stats.

Players can insure up to ten items (ten single items, not 10 stacks of items) by speaking to the [[Financial Wizard]] and depositing the items in the safe deposit box. Items in the safe deposit box will not be lost, unlike those found in the bank, and can be collected any time the player visits the Financial Wizard.

[[File:Deadman mode - Bank Raid interface.png|thumb|right|300px|The Bank Raid interface.]]

cases.name: Intelligence
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Intelligence detail.png|left|160px]]
'''Intelligence''' is obtained from [[gangster]]s and the [[gang boss]] during one of their meetings, which can be discovered by speaking to [[Captain Ginea]]. It can be given to her in exchange for a [[training manual]]. This is part of the [[Intelligence Gathering]] activity.

This item cannot be banked, and will instead message ''"A magical force prevents you from banking this item!"'' upon attempt.

cases.name: Training manual
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Training manual detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''training manual''' is obtained from [[Captain Ginea]] as part of the [[Intelligence Gathering]] activity after giving her an [[intelligence]] report, dropped by [[gangster]]s and the [[gang boss]] during one of their meetings. Reading the book gives the player the option to gain experience in either [[Hitpoints]], [[Attack]], [[Strength]], or [[Defence]]. This item cannot be banked. Dying with the book in your inventory will cause it to be permanently lost.

cases.name: Servery pineapple pizza
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Servery pineapple pizza detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Servery pineapple pizza''' is obtained from using [[servery pineapple chunks]] on a [[servery plain pizza]]. It is then served at the buffet table for the [[Shayzien]] soldiers in the [[Hosidius]] [[mess]]. A [[Cooking]] level of 65 is required to make this pizza. This item cannot be banked.

cases.name: Gricoller's fertiliser
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Gricoller's fertiliser detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Gricoller's fertiliser''' is an item only available within the [[Tithe Farm]] [[minigame]].

It is automatically added to your inventory at the start of the minigame granted the player has enough space.

After being used on a planted seed, it will decrease the time it takes for the seed to grow by half.

Gricoller's fertiliser can be useful at the end of a Tithe Farm session when only a small number of fruit are needed to hit the bonus points at the 100 fruit threshold; the fertiliser will help speed up the last growth periods of the smaller batches of plants.

{{Tithe Farm}}

cases.name: Golovanova seed
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Golovanova seed detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Golovanova seeds''' are used to grow [[golovanova fruit]] in the [[Tithe Farm]] [[minigame]]. Level 34 [[Farming]] is required to use the seeds.

Upon leaving the minigame area through the [[farm door]], all seeds in a player's inventory will disappear.

No experience is granted for planting the seeds. The player will receive 6 experience upon harvesting the fruit and 60 experience for depositing it into the sacks, or 6.1 and 61.5 experience respectively with the complete [[farmer's outfit]]. The player will also receive a bonus of 1,500 experience should they return 75 fruit or more at a time. This experience bonus is not boosted by the farmer's oufit. Additionally, the 75th through 100th fruit deposited will grant double experience. Up to 10,000 seeds can be obtained from the table by the entrance of the minigame.

The total experience earned from harvesting and depositing a full batch of seeds (100 fruits) is 9,660. Wearing the full farmer's outfit will boost the experience from harvesting and depositing fruit (but not the experience bonus) by 2.5%, bringing the total experience per 100 fruits to 9,859.

Leaving the Tithe Farm minigame, either through the door, teleporting, or any other means, will remove any harvested fruit from the players inventory, and reward 0 xp. However, the player can safely log out without losing any harvested fruit or seeds, as the player will be placed inside the minigame when logged back in.

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Stolen pendant detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''stolen pendant''' is obtained by [[stealing artefacts]] from houses in the residential district in [[Port Piscarilius]], requiring 49 [[Thieving]]. Successfully picking the lock to the [[drawers (stealing artefacts)|drawers]] and retrieving the stolen pendant yields 750 Thieving [[experience]]. It is given to [[Captain Khaled]] for {{NoCoins|500}}-{{NoCoins|1000}} coins and additional Thieving experience equal to 40x the player's Thieving level.

Teleporting or logging out after acquiring the stolen pendant, but before delivering it, will remove the pendant from the player's inventory forcing them to report to Khaled that the item was lost and a new task is needed. 

According to Captain Khaled, the stolen artefacts are shipped overseas.{{CiteNPC|npc=Captain Khaled|quote=We specialise in 'acquiring' valuable antiquities from around the city and shipping them to our friends overseas.}}

cases.name: Dense essence block
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dense essence block detail.png|left|120px]]
A '''dense essence block''' is a raw material used in the [[Runecraft]] skill to make [[blood rune]]s, [[soul rune]]s, and [[Arceuus spellbook]] [[teleport tablet]]s. They can be obtained by mining the [[dense runestone]] at the [[dense essence mine]] north-east of [[Arceuus]].

Dense essence blocks can be infused with dark power at the [[Dark Altar]] found north-west of the dense runestone mines, turning every dense essence block in the player's inventory into a [[dark essence block]]. One Prayer point is drained for each block converted, however players '''can''' still convert blocks with 0 Prayer points remaining.

The dark essence blocks can then be crushed with a [[chisel]] to turn into [[dark essence fragments]]. These dark essence fragments can then be used for runecrafting blood and soul runes. Alternatively, the dark essence blocks can be brought to the lectern located in the [[Ouditor]]'s house in [[Arceuus]] to create teleport tablets.

Dense essence blocks and dark essence fragments cannot be banked, however dark essence blocks can.

Players cannot get the [[rock golem]] pet while mining dense essence blocks.

cases.name: Blasted ore
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Blasted ore detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Blasted ore''' is obtained after detonating a hard rock face in the [[blast mine]]. Players must first excavate the hard rock using a [[chisel]], then using a pot of [[dynamite]] on the resulting cavity. Then, players must light the dynamite and run away from it, or large amounts of damage will be taken.

Once the dynamite explodes, blasted ore will appear where the dynamite exploded. It should then be deposited in an ore sack near a blonde-haired [[operator]]. Players have three minutes before the blasted ore disintegrates, so it is encouraged to deposit the ore frequently.

Should the player pick up but not deposit the blasted ore in the Ore sack in time, the blasted ore will disappear from the inventory and a message will appear in the chat interface "Your blasted ore has disintegrated." Hopping worlds will also cause all blasted ore to disintegrate.

If a temporary boost is to be applied when blast mining, they must be activated before the blasted ore is initially spawned.

Like [[pay-dirt]], blasted ore cannot be deposited in a [[bank]].

cases.name: Satchel
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Satchel detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''Satchel''' is obtained during [[Monkey Madness II]]. After navigating the maze, the player will discover a [[crate (Monkey Madness II, satchel)|crate]] which they can search. The player needs a total of six satchels to complete that section of the quest. After six are obtained, the player must re-navigate the maze to find the [[barrel (Monkey Madness II, explosive)|explosives]] which can only be stored within the satchel.

After all the explosive satchels are placed at weak point, the player can leave the construction site and detonate the explosives.

These satchels cannot be banked.

cases.name: Elysian spirit shield
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Elysian spirit shield (Monkey Madness II) detail.png|left|150px]]
The '''elysian spirit shield''' is an [[Items|item]] which can be retrieved from [[Nieve]]'s remains during [[Monkey Madness II]] after [[Glough]] becomes mutated. The shield disintegrated as a result of Glough's devastating attack on the Slayer master.

It serves as a joke item, as the [[Elysian spirit shield|real shield]] is widely coveted among high level players. There are no uses for the ruined shield, and it cannot be deposited into a [[bank]]. The ruined shield is always lost on death.

cases.name: Bruma root
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bruma root detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''bruma root''' is obtained by chopping [[bruma roots]] found in the four corners of the [[Wintertodt]]'s prison north of the [[Wintertodt Camp]]. The experience given is equal to 0.3 times the player's [[Woodcutting]] level. They cannot be taken out of the prison.

It is burned in a [[brazier]] which drains the Wintertodt's energy, granting [[Firemaking]] experience equal to 3x the player's level per log. These can be [[Fletching|fletched]] into [[bruma kindling]]s, which give 3.8x the player's Firemaking level in experience, roughly 27% more. The [[fletching knife]] works on the bruma roots, speeding up the rate at which they are fletched.

cases.name: Bruma kindling
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bruma kindling detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''bruma kindling''' is obtained by using a [[knife]] on a [[bruma root]], granting [[Fletching]] experience appropriate to the player's level. The Fletching experience given is equal to 0.6 times the player's Fletching level.

It is used to burn the braziers, found in the four corners of the [[Wintertodt]]'s prison, to drain the Wintertodt's energy, granting [[Firemaking]] experience appropriate to the player's level. Bruma kindlings give approximately 27% more [[Firemaking]] experience than using [[bruma root]]s on the [[brazier]], 3.8 times the player's Firemaking level. When using the [[Fletching knife]], the fletching time is reduced by 1 [[tick]] starting from the second action onward. This represents an average fletching speed increase of 15-30% depending on Wintertodt attacks, most likely around 20%.

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Rejuvenation potion (unf) detail.png|left|120px]]
A '''rejuvenation potion (unf)''' is an unfinished potion obtained from the [[Crate (Wintertodt)|crate]] found in the [[Wintertodt]]'s prison north of the [[Wintertodt Camp]].

It is used to make the [[rejuvenation potion]] by adding a [[bruma herb]], earning [[Herblore]] [[experience]] appropriate to the player's level.

cases.name: Bruma herb
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bruma herb detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Bruma herbs''' are obtained from picking [[Sprouting Roots]] found within the lobby and the east and west side of the [[Wintertodt]]'s prison. They are used on a [[rejuvenation potion (unf)]] to create a [[rejuvenation potion]], yielding [[Herblore]] experience equal to 10% of the player's Herblore level. They can be used to heal the [[pyromancer]]s and to restore player's warmth during a game of Wintertodt.

cases.sourceContext:
{{Synced switch

'''Rejuvenation potions''' are created by adding a [[bruma herb]] to a [[rejuvenation potion (unf)]], earning [[Herblore]] [[experience]] equal to the player's Herblore level divided by 10.

Each potion holds 4 doses and are used to heal the [[pyromancer]]s found in the [[Wintertodt]]'s prison. Using a dose on a pyromancer heals them fully and grants the player 75 points towards a [[reward cart]] roll when subduing the Wintertodt. A single dose will fully heal any pyromancer, including those that have been incapacitated. When healing pyromancers, a dose will be consumed from the potion with the fewest doses remaining.

You are able to drink this potion to restore 30% of your own [[Wintertodt#Fighting the Wintertodt|warmth]].

[[Brew'ma]] can create the potions for the player if they wish not to do it themselves or haven't completed [[Druidic Ritual]], provided the player gives them the ingredients.

Attempting to create this potion outside of the Wintertodt's prison results in the message {{mes|You can only do that within the influence of the Bruma tree.}} appearing in the chatbox.

cases.name: Dark relic
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dark relic detail.png|left|150px]]
The '''dark relic''' is a possible reward from the [[Chambers of Xeric]]. It has a ''Commune'' option which will result in the chat box stating ''A dark power emanates from the relic. You sense that this power can be directed.''

Upon communing with the relic, the player may choose a [[Skills|skill]] in which to receive [[experience]]. If the chosen skill is one of the skills used in the Chambers of Xeric – [[combat]] skills, [[Mining]], [[Woodcutting]], [[Herblore]], [[Farming]], [[Hunter]], [[Cooking]], [[Fishing]], [[Thieving]], [[Firemaking]], or [[Agility]] – the player will receive 150 times their level in that skill as experience. If the chosen skill is not on this list, the player will instead only receive 50 times the corresponding skill level as experience. [[Construction]] is not included in the list of skills that receive an additional experience bonus, despite it being used to build [[storage unit]]s.

cases.name: Heat-proof vessel
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Heat-proof vessel detail.png|left|140px]]
A '''heat-proof vessel''' (also referred to as a '''large water container''' for the upgrade in the [[Collection Log]] and [[Petrified Pete's Ore Shop]]) is a water container given to the player by [[Petrified Pete]] upon entering the [[Volcanic Mine]]. It can be equipped in the weapon slot. It has 36 uses per game, and can be used to throw water onto the lava, creating platforms which players can walk on. These platforms will melt after 90 seconds, giving players limited time to stand on them. If players remain on the hardened lava when it melts, they will fall into the lava, taking massive damage.

The water can only be thrown while the player is facing north, east, south, and west. Additionally, the water canteen can be right-clicked to open a dialogue box to throw water in a specified direction, or right-clicked while it is equipped to select the direction the player wants to throw it at.

Players can purchase the large water container upgrade from Petrified Pete 10,000 Volcanic Mine points to allow the vessel to hold more water, increasing the number of uses per game from 36 to 72.

cases.name: Large rock
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Large rock detail.png|left|150px]]
A '''large rock''' is used in the [[Volcanic Mine]] to increase the gas pressure by blocking [[Volcanic chamber|gas chambers]]. Should the gas pressure be too high, players should mine the [[blocked volcanic chamber|blockage]] to reduce the pressure and maintain the mine's stability.

Players cannot take the rock out of the mine, as it will disappear upon leaving. However, should players die in the mine with the rock in their possession, it can be smuggled out of the mine by reclaiming the player's lost items from [[Petrified Pete]], but note that the rock cannot be deposited into the [[bank]].

[[File:Antique lamp (fossil display) detail.png|left|180px]]
The '''antique lamp''' is an item obtained from completing [[fossil display]]s in the [[Varrock Museum]].

A small display will give an antique lamp that grants 2,000 experience (Level 20 or higher) in a skill, a medium display will give 3,500 experience (Level 30 or higher), and a large/plant display will give 5,000 experience (Level 35 or higher), which, if all the displays are completed, adds up to 120,000 experience.

{{Experience lamp}}

cases.name: Pufferfish
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Pufferfish detail.png|160px|left]]
A '''pufferfish''' can be caught [[underwater]] on [[Fossil Island]]. They can be held in a player's inventory to reduce a player's weight by 0.5kg, and can be used via a "Puff" option to restore 15% oxygen to stay underwater for longer.

Using the ''Puff'' action produces the message {{Mes|You depuff the pufferfish, restoring some of your puff.}}. They are then released back into the water as a [[Puffer Fish]] which will [[retreat]] from the player and appear deflated for several minutes before being able to be caught again. If the player has a [[fishbowl helmet]] or a [[medallion of the deep]] equipped, it cannot be puffed, stating that {{Mes|You ineffectually squash the poor puffer fish against your helmet.}} or {{Mes|That didn't help.}} if only the medallion is equipped. 

The ''Drop'' action produces the text {{Mes|You release the pufferfish.}} In this case, it will not be deflated or retreat from the player and can be caught again immediately.

Upon returning to the surface, all pufferfish in the player's possession will disappear.

Attempting to drop a pufferfish above water results in the message {{Mes|The poor pufferfish expires with a lack of access to the sea.}}.

cases.name: Letter
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Letter (The Queen of Thieves) detail.png|left|100px]]
A '''letter''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used only in [[The Queen of Thieves]]. It is found in a locked chest, that can pickpocketed, on the {{Floornumber|uk=1}} floor of [[Councillor Hughes]]' home in [[Kingstown]].

It is given to [[Tomas Lawry]] so he can arrange for her arrest.

cases.name: Fine mesh net
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Fine mesh net detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''Fine mesh net''' is an item obtained in [[Santa]]'s Grotto during the [[2017 Christmas event]]. It is used to catch [[Snow Sprite]]s to light up [[Dolph]]'s nose.

After the event is completed, it was automatically taken away from the player. However, players could reobtain it by revisiting the [[Land of Snow]] via speaking to the [[Wise Old Man]] after completing the event. After the event ended, it was automatically deleted from every player.

It cannot be used as a [[Butterfly net|net]] for [[butterfly (Hunter)|butterflies]] or [[implings]], even if it is reobtained after the event.

cases.name: Glistening tear
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Glistening tear detail.png|left|100px]]
'''Glistening tears''' are a form of currency found in the [[Underwater Agility and Thieving]] training activity, located in the [[Underwater]] section of [[Fossil Island]]. Glistening tears can be exchanged with [[Mairin]] for experience in [[Agility]], [[Thieving]], or both, and are obtained by looting [[Chest (underwater)|chest]]s and [[clam]]s during the activity. Glistening tears are always obtained alongside a [[mermaid's tear]]. Approximately 150 tears are obtainable per hour.

The most efficient way of exchanging glistening tears is selecting both skills. While it gives less experience in an individual skill, its value is higher than training the two skills independently, due to Agility being proportionally slower to train.

Players can only exchange a maximum of 700 glistening tears at once; if players exchange them for experience with more than 700 glistening tears in the inventory, the excess will be '''discarded'''. In addition, they cannot be deposited into a [[bank]].

[[File:Vial of blood (A Taste of Hope) detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''vial of blood''' is obtained during [[A Taste of Hope]] by giving [[Safalaan]] an empty [[vial]]. The vial contains his blood, which is used to create a [[blood potion]].

cases.name: Flaygian's notes
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Flaygian's notes detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Flaygian's notes''' are obtained during [[A Taste of Hope]]. They are the results of [[Flaygian Screwte]]'s effort to translate the [[Haemalchemy]] book that the player found during [[Darkness of Hallowvale]]. A '''coin pouch''' is an item obtained from [[pickpocketing]] certain [[NPC]]s, which contains several [[coins]] depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the [[Ardougne Diary]], where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via [[Thieving training#Levels 45-55/91: Blackjacking|blackjacking]] yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If [[rogue equipment]] is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

A '''coin pouch''' is an item obtained from [[pickpocketing]] certain [[NPC]]s, which contains several [[coins]] depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the [[Ardougne Diary]], where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via [[Thieving training#Levels 45-55/91: Blackjacking|blackjacking]] yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If [[rogue equipment]] is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

A '''coin pouch''' is an item obtained from [[pickpocketing]] certain [[NPC]]s, which contains several [[coins]] depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the [[Ardougne Diary]], where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via [[Thieving training#Levels 45-55/91: Blackjacking|blackjacking]] yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If [[rogue equipment]] is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

cases.name: Antique lamp
Antique lamp
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Antique lamp (A Kingdom Divided) detail.png|left|180px]]
The '''antique lamp''' is a reward from [[A Kingdom Divided]], two of which are received from [[Commander Fullore]] upon completing the [[quest]]. Each lamp grants 10,000 [[experience]] in a [[skill]] of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 40.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from Commander Fullore whenever the player wishes to do so. If you die with it in inventory Commander Fullore will grant the lamps.

Players who have completed the removed [[Architectural Alliance]] miniquest prior to [[10 January]] [[2024]] without claiming an antique lamp as their reward can still do so.

cases.name: Mimic
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Mimic detail.png|left|140px]]
The '''Mimic''' is an item that may be obtained when attempting to open an [[Reward casket (elite)|elite]] or [[Reward casket (master)|master reward casket]]. In order to be eligible to obtain it, players must first speak to the [[strange casket]] upstairs in [[Watson's house]] in [[Hosidius]] to enable the chance of a reward casket turning into the Mimic; attempting to open an elite or master reward casket for the first time before speaking to the strange casket will direct players to the strange casket if they say they want Mimic encounters. An [[Reward casket (elite)|elite reward casket]] has a 1/35 chance of being a mimic, while [[Reward casket (master)|master reward caskets]] have a 1/15 chance.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Wolf|url=https://twitter.com/JagexWolf/status/1116299462870274048|date=11 April 2019|archiveurl=https://archive.is/ogJGw|archivedate=28 May 2020|quote=We will be changing the rate of The Mimic chance after a discussion with the team and your feedback that it may be a tad too rare. We will be keeping an eye on the frequency over the coming days, but these are the new rates which will be live shortly: Master: 1/15 Elite: 1/35|name=mimicodds}} There is a dry protection that guarantees your first Mimic encounter on either the 10th master reward casket or 25th elite reward casket, if you have Mimic encounters enabled. 

When obtained, a message in the chatbox will state {{mes|The chest turned out to be the Mimic!}}. Attempting to open the Mimic before defeating the Mimic boss gives the message "Visit the Strange Casket, upstairs in Watson's house in Hosidius, to attempt the Mimic's challenge.".

Once a player obtains the Mimic, they can return to the strange casket to challenge [[The Mimic]]. When the player defeats the Mimic, they must leave in order to open the mimic chest and receive their reward. If a player attempts to open the mimic chest while in the Mimic's fight area, the chatbox will state ''"It'd be bad taste to try opening that in here."''

If a player tries to open another elite or master reward casket with a Mimic in the player's inventory, the chatbox will warn the player "You already have a Mimic, and cannot be given another one. Do you wish to open the casket anyway?" {{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1625816702532435971|date=15 February 2023|archiveurl=https://archive.is/6eiuA|archivedate=14 March 2023|quote=You can only have one at a time. If you already do have one, the game warns you: “You already have a Mimic, and cannot be given another one. Do you wish to open the casket anyway?”|name=mimicwarning}} However, if the Mimic is dropped on the ground, the player may obtain more Mimics. Just like clue scrolls, Mimics can be [[Guide:Clue Juggling|juggled]], staying on the ground for an hour before despawning. As such the player may opt to juggle Mimics if opening a lot of caskets. Once done, the player can pick up all Mimics at once, since there is no restriction against carrying several Mimics.

The Mimic cannot be deposited into a bank. If players try to bank it, the chatbox will state ''"A magical force prevents you from banking this item!"''

When opening your first casket after defeating The Mimic you will also be given a [[Mimic scroll case]] which can be opened to let you stack 1 more [[Scroll box]] for every tier of clue scroll.

cases.name: Lamp of knowledge
Hand mirror
Imbued tephra
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Imbued tephra detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Imbued tephra''' is obtained by imbuing [[refined tephra]] at the [[Altar (Zalcano)|Seren altar]] in the western end of [[Zalcano]]'s prison. It can also be obtained from [[golem (Zalcano)|golem]]s that Zalcano occasionally summons.

The imbued tephra is the only item that can deal damage to Zalcano while she is still standing; the damage dealt is scaled based on the player's [[Smithing]] and [[Runecraft]] levels. In addition, if she has summoned [[demonic symbol]]s around the prison, the blue symbols will increase the damage dealt. Players can either attack Zalcano directly while having the imbued tephra in their inventory to use them, or equip and throw them at her.

cases.name: Fang
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Fang (The Fremennik Exiles) detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''fang''' is an item found during the [[The Fremennik Exiles]] quest, obtained by searching the rocks west of the [[sandpit]] in [[Rellekka]]. It is given to [[Freygerd]] along with the [[unsealed letter]] and [[venom gland]] as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka.

The item's model appears to be based off the [[magic fang]], without the purple orb.

cases.name: Venom gland
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Venom gland detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''Venom gland''' is an item used in [[The Fremennik Exiles]] quest. It can be found in some crates south of the house that is south of the [[sandpit]] in [[Rellekka]]. It is given to [[Freygerd]] along with the [[Fang (The Fremennik Exiles)|fang]] and an [[unsealed letter]] as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka.

cases.name: Unsealed letter
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Unsealed letter detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''unsealed letter''' is an item used in [[The Fremennik Exiles]] quest. It is obtained by killing a [[Basilisk Youngling]] that comes out after the player searches the [[sandpit]] in [[Rellekka]]. It is given to [[Freygerd]] along with the [[Fang (The Fremennik Exiles)|fang]] and [[venom gland]] as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka, and if the player has not read it, it is returned by [[Brundt the Chieftain]].

cases.name: Unsealed letter
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Unsealed letter detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''unsealed letter''' is an item used in [[The Fremennik Exiles]] quest. It is obtained by killing a [[Basilisk Youngling]] that comes out after the player searches the [[sandpit]] in [[Rellekka]]. It is given to [[Freygerd]] along with the [[Fang (The Fremennik Exiles)|fang]] and [[venom gland]] as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka, and if the player has not read it, it is returned by [[Brundt the Chieftain]].

cases.name: Birthday cake
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Birthday cake (Mobile Anniversary) detail.png|left|100px]]
The '''birthday cake''' is an item obtained from the large cakes in [[Varrock Square]] in commemoration of the [[Mobile Anniversary|first anniversary]] of [[Old School RuneScape Mobile]]. Eating the cake heals six [[hitpoints]]. There is no limit to the number of slices players can take from the fountain, aside from inventory size. While they are tradeable, they cannot be sold on the [[Grand Exchange]].

Taking a slice from the fountain for the first time after logging in causes the chatbox to display a message: ''"You can take this slice of cake just about anywhere with you, just like OSRS Mobile!"''

Players using the desktop client can right-click the cake and click the "Learn-more" option, which prompts a confirmation message to open [https://www.oldschool.runescape.com/mobile this link] in the player's browser. If players select the "Learn-more" option on the mobile version, the chatbox will state ''"You are currently playing on mobile. You seem to know what you are doing!"''
[[File:Mobile Anniversary.png|thumb|left|300px|Varrock Square's fountain transformed into four giant slices of cake.]]

cases.name: Lamp of the Gatherer
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Lamp of the Gatherer detail.png|180px|left]]
The '''Lamp of the Gatherer''' is an item obtained from [[Adventurer Jon]] by completing tasks in the [[Adventure Paths]]' Gatherer Path. It grants 150 [[experience]] in either [[Fishing]], [[Mining]] or [[Woodcutting]].

cases.name: Painted fake magic egg
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Painted fake magic egg detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''painted fake magic egg''' is an item obtained during the [[2020 Easter event]] by dipping an [[unpainted fake magic egg]] in [[paint buckets]] found on top of the Castle in [[Bunbridge]].

The player must try to deceive [[Duke Rabbacio]] to replace his [[Magic Egg]] with the fake one by asking the magic egg if it itself is the fake one.

cases.name: Unpainted fake magic egg
Conch shell
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Conch shell detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''conch shell''' was an item found on south-west side of [[Bunbridge]] in the [[2020 Easter event]]. It was formerly used on a [[broken egg]] to create an [[unpainted fake magic egg]].

cases.name: Broken egg
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Broken egg detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''broken egg''' is an item obtained during the [[2020 Easter event]], from [[Farmer Maggot]]'s farm on the north-east side of [[Bunbridge]]. It is used on a [[conch shell]] to create an [[unpainted fake magic egg]].

cases.name: Carrot
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Carrot detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''carrot''' was an orange item used for the post-[[2020 Easter event]] pseudo-quest, [[2020 Easter event#Mini Quest - The Rabbit's Assistant|The Rabbit's Assistant]]. It was found on a table in a house south of the [[Rabbit Realm]] Castle, and is one of three ingredients players must give the [[Rabbit Chef]].

cases.name: Broken goat horn
Cake
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Cake (2020 Easter event) detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''cake''' is an item that is used for the post-[[2020 Easter event]] pseudo-quest, [[2020 Easter event#Mini Quest - The Rabbit's Assistant|The Rabbit's Assistant]]. It can be found at the Rabbit campfire at the north-west corner of [[Bunbridge]], and is one of three ingredients players must give the [[Rabbit Chef]].

While it shares the same appearance and examine as a regular [[cake]], it cannot be eaten.
{{2020 Easter event}}

cases.name: Tome of Experience
cases.sourceTitle: Tome of Experience (Sins of the Father)
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Tome of Experience (Sins of the Father) detail.png|left|130px]]
The '''tome of experience''' is received from [[Ivan Strom]] on completion of the [[Sins of the Father]] [[quest]]. Reading it opens a window to select the [[skill]] a player wishes to advance. The player must be at least level 60 in their chosen skill. In the event this item is lost or destroyed, players may reclaim this item from [[Ivan Strom]] in [[Old Man Ral]]'s house in [[Meiyerditch]]. After progressing far enough into [[The Blood Moon Rises]], it is reclaimed from Old Man Ral instead.

It has six chapters which provide 15,000 experience each. After confirming, the player receives the message "''You read a fascinating chapter and earn experience! You have been awarded 15,000 (skill) experience!''" After the sixth reading, the book disappears and the player receives the message "''The book crumbles into a dust cloud of knowledge.''"

This item cannot be banked. If your inventory is full, he will hold the tome for you until you clear some space and talk to him again.

cases.name: Spider snack
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Spider snack detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Spider snacks''' were used during the [[2020 Halloween event]]. It was obtained by searching the barrel of spiders at [[Eve (2020 Halloween event)|Eve's]] party. Players must eat one in order to have Eve help them with Rick's predicament. Despite being edible and described as tasty, they do not heal any hitpoints when eaten.

When eaten, the chatbox will state "''You eat the spider snack. It makes you feel surprisingly comfortable.''" If the player tries to use the spider snack on a [[range]] or [[fire]], the chatbox will state "''You can't cook that.''"

cases.name: Soul fragment
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Soul fragment detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Soul fragments''' are obtained as drops from [[Forgotten Soul (Soul Wars)|Forgotten Soul]]s during a game of [[Soul Wars]]. They can also be obtained by killing players who possess them. Players can give souls to team members with the use option.

The fragments are used on the [[Soul Obelisk]] to reduce the damage reduction percentage of the [[Avatar of Creation]] and [[Avatar of Destruction|Destruction]]. The team who controls the Soul Obelisk will have each soul fragment reduce the Avatar's damage reduction percentage by one, while the team that does not have control will find that sacrificing soul fragments at the Soul Obelisk will only be worth one-third of the contribution.

cases.name: Bones
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bones (Soul Wars) detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Bones''' are acquired in the [[Soul Wars]] [[minigame]] as drops from enemy players. They look just like [[bones|normal bones]], but have a different [[examine]] text and a [[destroy]] option instead of [[drop]].

The bones are buried at a graveyard to increase the percentage of their Avatar's damage reduction. If the bones are buried in a graveyard in which the team that does not have control over, it will only be worth one-third of the contribution. Players can also give the bones to a teammate by using it on them, providing the teammate has turned on [[Accept Aid]].

Players that die in Soul Wars will drop one set of bones, plus all of the bones and [[soul fragment]]s in their inventory.

When a game of Soul Wars ends, all gameplay items obtained are removed.

Burying the bones does not grant [[Prayer]] experience.

The sled is only useable in this instance; if a player attempts to ride the sled anywhere else, the chatbox will state ''"You cannot use that here!"''

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Red fireflies (item) detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Red fireflies''' are an item from the [[2020 Christmas event]]. They were obtained by catching [[red fireflies]] in the cave below the [[Goblin Village]]. Along with [[Green fireflies (item)|green fireflies]], they were given to the goblin generals during the event.

If lost, the item could be reobtained by catching one again before completing the event.

If lost, the item could be reobtained by catching one again before completing the event.

If lost, the item may be reobtained by searching the treasure chest again.

cases.name: Raw harpoonfish
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Raw harpoonfish detail.png|left|150px]]
'''Raw harpoonfish''' are fish that can be fished from [[Fishing spot (Tempoross Cove)|fishing spots]] in [[Tempoross Cove]]. During the fight with [[Tempoross]], they are used as ammunition for harpoonfish cannons. They can be [[harpoonfish|cooked]] at the [[Shrine (Tempoross Cove)|shrine]], which allows them to drain Tempoross' energy more than raw ones. Catching a harpoonfish grants 5 points during the Tempoross fight. 

Note: You can use Tempoross harpoonfish in order to perform the initial [[Barbarian Training#Barehanded fishing|barehanded fishing]] task from [[Otto Godblessed]].

cases.name: Harpoonfish
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Harpoonfish detail.png|left|150px]]
'''Harpoonfish''' are obtained by cooking [[raw harpoonfish]]. They are used as ammunition for the [[harpoonfish cannon]]s during the fight against [[Tempoross]]. Cooked harpoonfish drain Tempoross' energy more than raw harpoonfish, as well as giving more points. They cannot be burnt.

According to the [[Spirit anglers research notes]], "cooking the Harpoonfish, while doing nothing for the edibility, does harden the bill, making them even more effective when used as ammunition."

cases.name: Crystallised harpoonfish
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Crystallised harpoonfish detail.png|left|150px]]
'''Crystallised harpoonfish''' are fish that can be fished from [[Fishing spot (Tempoross Cove)|fishing spots]] in [[Tempoross Cove]]. While fishing with a [[crystal harpoon]], there is a 1 in 3 chance that players will catch a crystallised harpoonfish instead of a raw one.

During the fight with [[Tempoross]], they are used as ammunition for harpoonfish cannons. Crystallised harpoonfish drains Tempoross' energy as much as raw ones, and cannot be cooked. While this means players will get fewer points over the course of the fight, players will instead receive 20% more Fishing experience from using them as ammunition.

cases.name: Heat-proof vessel
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Heat-proof vessel detail.png|left|140px]]
A '''heat-proof vessel''' (also referred to as a '''large water container''' for the upgrade in the [[Collection Log]] and [[Petrified Pete's Ore Shop]]) is a water container given to the player by [[Petrified Pete]] upon entering the [[Volcanic Mine]]. It can be equipped in the weapon slot. It has 36 uses per game, and can be used to throw water onto the lava, creating platforms which players can walk on. These platforms will melt after 90 seconds, giving players limited time to stand on them. If players remain on the hardened lava when it melts, they will fall into the lava, taking massive damage.

The water can only be thrown while the player is facing north, east, south, and west. Additionally, the water canteen can be right-clicked to open a dialogue box to throw water in a specified direction, or right-clicked while it is equipped to select the direction the player wants to throw it at.

Players can purchase the large water container upgrade from Petrified Pete 10,000 Volcanic Mine points to allow the vessel to hold more water, increasing the number of uses per game from 36 to 72.

cases.name: Bandages
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bandages (Theatre of Blood) detail.png|left|100px]]
'''Bandages''' are a consumable item obtainable during the [[Theatre of Blood]] [[Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode|entry mode]]. They restore 20 hitpoints, a variable amount of prayer points,{{clarify|This is a value that scales with prayer level; more research is needed.}}  and 20% run energy when consumed. They also cure poison, boost the player's combat stats, and provide the effect of a [[stamina potion]].

Bandages act as a food item, and therefore delay the player's next attack when consumed during combat. They can be [[combo eat]]en with potions and/or [[cooked karambwan]].

10 bandages can be claimed from the rewards chest after defeating the [[Pestilent Bloat]] and another 10 become available after defeating [[Sotetseg]]. The chest can only contain a maximum of 10 bandages, so uncollected bandages are deleted.

Stat boosts to Attack, Strength and Defence are one level lower than the corresponding super potion, and are calculated with: <math display="inline">\lfloor SkillLevel \times \frac{15}{100} \rfloor + 4</math>

Ranged boost is equal to a [[ranging potion]], and is calculated with: <math display="inline">\lfloor SkillLevel \times \frac{1}{10} \rfloor + 4</math>

Magic boost is a static +4, equal to a [[magic potion]].
