The '''Shayzien journal''' is an old journal written by King Shayzien VII, who ruled [[Great Kourend]] from the 32nd to 37th decade. Recovered from the [[Tower of Magic]] during the uprising against [[Xeric]] at the end of the [[Age of Strife]], it was sent via parcel by an unknown party to [[Phileas Rimor]]'s house, and kickstarts the events of the [[quest]] [[Tale of the Righteous]].

During [[A Kingdom Divided]], the journal is recovered from [[Lord Kandur Hosidius]]' hidden office at the request of [[Lord Shiro Shayzien]]. It is revealed later in the quest that it was Lord Hosidius who had acquired the journal and sent the parcel to Phileas, while the journal players took from his office was actually just a copy with many bits removed.

When read, the chatbox message states ''The old journal seems to have been bound shut somehow. Maybe Lord Shayzien will know what to do with it.''

{{A Kingdom Divided}}

cases.name: Pumpkin pie
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Pumpkin pie detail.png|left|120px]]
The '''pumpkin pie''' is an [[unobtainable item]] used during the [[2021 Halloween event]]. In order to distract the [[Cook (Blue Moon Inn)|Cook]] in the [[Blue Moon Inn]], the player orders this meal and loudly insults the food, causing the chef to leave the kitchen.

Although the item can be seen on a table during the cutscene, it cannot actually be obtained. Ending the cutscene with an empty inventory slot will cause the player to receive a [[pie dish]].

The item could originally be bought and sold on the [[Grand Exchange]] due to an oversight, but was never listed on the [[Grand Exchange Database]]. Some people were able to obtain the Pumpkin pie through glitches, and sell it for very high prices. As a result of this exploit, it was made untradeable in a hotfix, then delisted from the Grand Exchange altogether. 

With the end of the event, the pie was removed from the inventories of any players who still had them. However, they were not removed from any uncollected Grand Exchange offers, and are therefore still in the game.

If players attempt to make scary sounds with it before climbing a tree, the chatbox will state "''I should wait until I'm in a tree to do this!''" If players destroy the bottle at crucial moments when trying to scare Oziach, the chatbox will state "''You destroyed the bottle, meaning you have no way of scaring Oziach anymore.''" and the player returns to their former location.

cases.name: Guardian fragments
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Guardian fragments detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Guardian fragments''' are remnants of rune guardians that are mined during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. They can be used on the workbench at the [[Temple of the Eye (location)|Temple of the Eye]] to create [[guardian essence]], which are then crafted upon [[runic altar]]s to create [[Elemental guardian stone|elemental]] or [[catalytic guardian stone]]s.

cases.name: Guardian essence
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Guardian essence detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Guardian essence''' is an item obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. Guardian essence can be stored in [[essence pouch]]es. This item can be obtained by using [[guardian fragments]] on the [[Workbench (Guardians of the Rift)|workbench]] in the [[Guardians of the Rift]] minigame. Alternatively, this item can be obtained by mining the [[huge guardian remains]] or [[fallen guardian]]s which provide essence rather than fragments like the other [[guardian remains]].

cases.name: Catalytic guardian stone
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Catalytic guardian stone detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Catalytic guardian stones''' are items used to power-up [[the Great Guardian]] during a game of [[Guardians of the Rift]], alongside [[elemental guardian stone]]s and [[polyelemental guardian stone]]s.

They are obtained by imbuing [[guardian essence]] at a [[Runic altar#Catalytic|catalytic runic altar]], accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. This is a 1:1 ratio of essence to stones. The Raiments of the Eye set does not offer additional bonuses. 

Players are granted 5 [[Runecraft]] experience and 2 catalytic energy per catalytic guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Mind, Body, Cosmic, Chaos, Nature, Law, Death and Blood Runes give Catalytic Energy.

cases.name: Elemental guardian stone
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Elemental guardian stone detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Elemental guardian stones''' are items used to power-up [[the Great Guardian]] during a game of [[Guardians of the Rift]], alongside [[catalytic guardian stone]]s and [[polyelemental guardian stone]]s.

They are obtained by imbuing [[guardian essence]] at an [[Runic altar#Elemental|elemental runic altar]], accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 [[Runecraft]] experience and 2 elemental energy per elemental guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Air, Water, Earth and Fire Runes give Elemental Energy.

cases.name: Uncharged cell
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Uncharged cell detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Uncharged cells''' are an item obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. They are charged by imbuing them at a [[Runic altar|runic altar]], accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. The type of charge it holds is dependent on the runic altar it is charged at.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "An uncharged magical cell built to hold runic energy."

cases.name: Weak cell
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Weak cell detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Weak cells''' are an item obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. Players can obtain one from the table by the entrance, or  by imbuing an [[uncharged cell]] at the [[Air Altar|Air]], [[Mind Altar|Mind]], or [[Body Altar]], which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The weak cell can be used alongside a [[chisel]] to create [[Weak elemental guardian|weak elemental]] and [[Weak catalytic guardian|catalytic guardians]] or placed on an [[inactive cell tile]] to create [[Weak Barrier|weak barriers]], or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A magical cell charged with a small amount of runic energy."

cases.name: Medium cell
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Medium cell detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Medium cells''' are an item obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. Players can obtain one by imbuing an [[uncharged cell]] at the [[Water Altar|Water]], [[Cosmic Altar|Cosmic]], or [[Chaos Altar]], which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The medium cell can be used alongside a [[chisel]] to create [[Medium elemental guardian|medium elemental]] and [[Medium catalytic guardian|catalytic guardians]], be placed on a [[weak cell tile]] to create [[Medium Barrier|medium barriers]], or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state {{mes|A magical cell charged with a moderate amount of runic energy.}}

cases.name: Strong cell
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Strong cell detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Strong cells''' are an item obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. Players can obtain one by imbuing an [[uncharged cell]] at the [[Earth Altar|Earth]], [[Nature Altar|Nature]], or [[Law Altar]], which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The strong cell can be used alongside a [[chisel]] to create [[Strong elemental guardian|strong elemental]] and [[Strong catalytic guardian|catalytic guardians]], be placed on a [[medium cell tile]] to create [[Strong Barrier|strong barriers]], or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A magical cell charged with a high amount of runic energy."

cases.name: Overcharged cell
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Overcharged cell detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Overcharged cells''' are items obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]]. Players can obtain one by imbuing an [[uncharged cell]] at the [[Fire Altar|Fire]], [[Death Altar|Death]], or [[Blood Altar]], which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The overcharged cell can be used alongside a [[chisel]] to create [[Overcharged elemental guardian|overcharged elemental]] and [[Overcharged catalytic guardian|catalytic guardians]]. They can also be placed on a [[strong cell tile]] to create [[Overcharged Barrier|overcharged barriers]], or reinforce existing ones.

When inspected, the chatbox will display a message similar to the cell's examine text, describing the cell as "a magical cell charged with an immense amount of runic energy."

cases.name: Portal talisman (air)
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Portal talisman (air) detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Air portal talismans''' are items that can be obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]], by imbuing [[guardian essence]] or charging [[uncharged cell]]s at the [[Air Altar]]. Upon receiving one, a message in the chatbox will state "''You discover a strange talisman during the runecrafting process!''"

Portal talismans have a 1/250 chance of being acquired per guardian essence crafted, or 1/200 if players have a [[Abyssal lantern (maple logs)|maple abyssal lantern]] equipped;{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1668137185898377217|date=12 June 2023|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/103167|archivedate=12 June 2023|quote=If I'm reading my colleagues' code correctly, it rolls 1/250 per rune obtained, until you get one [portal talisman]. That's buffed to 1/200 for the 20% boost.|notes=Mod Ash was partially incorrect in this deleted tweet; it rolls per guardian essence, rather than per rune. The next cited tweet references this clarification.}}{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1668580037145112580|date=13 June 2023|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/97784|archivedate=13 June 2023|quote=Oh, yeah, sorry - per essence.}} this chance is rolled until the player receives one.

The portal talisman can be used to enter the [[Guardian of Air]] to access the Air Altar, even if it is inactive. Doing so consumes the talisman, unless the Guardian of Air is currently active. Portal talismans cannot be kept after the game ends, so it is recommended to use them whenever possible.

Players can right-click "Toggle-talisman" on the Guardian of Air to toggle whether they wish to receive portal talismans or not from crafting at the Air Altar.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A talisman bound to a runic altar. Presenting this to the respective portal guardian will return you there."

'''Nature portal talismans''' are items that can be obtained during the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]], by imbuing [[guardian essence]] or charging [[uncharged cell]]s at the [[Nature Altar]]. Upon receiving one, a message in the chatbox will state "''You discover a strange talisman during the runecrafting process!''"

Portal talismans have a 1/250 chance of being acquired per guardian essence crafted, or 1/200 if players have a [[Abyssal lantern (maple logs)|maple abyssal lantern]] equipped;{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1668137185898377217|date=12 June 2023|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/103167|archivedate=12 June 2023|quote=If I'm reading my colleagues' code correctly, it rolls 1/250 per rune obtained, until you get one [portal talisman]. That's buffed to 1/200 for the 20% boost.|notes=Mod Ash was partially incorrect in this deleted tweet; it rolls per guardian essence, rather than per rune. The next cited tweet references this clarification.}}{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1668580037145112580|date=13 June 2023|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/97784|archivedate=13 June 2023|quote=Oh, yeah, sorry - per essence.}} this chance is rolled until the player receives one.

The portal talisman can be used to enter the [[Guardian of Nature]] to access the Nature Altar, even if it is inactive. Doing so consumes the talisman, unless the Guardian of Nature is currently active. Portal talismans cannot be kept after the game ends, so it is recommended to use them whenever possible.

Players can right-click "Toggle-talisman" on the Guardian of Nature to toggle whether they wish to receive portal talismans or not from crafting at the Nature Altar.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A talisman bound to a runic altar. Presenting this to the respective portal guardian will return you there."

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Polyelemental guardian stone detail.png|left|120px]]
'''Polyelemental guardian stones''' are items used to power-up [[the Great Guardian]] during a game of [[Guardians of the Rift]], alongside [[elemental guardian stone|elemental]], [[catalytic guardian stone|catalytic]], and [[Polycatalytic guardian stone|polycatalytic]] guardian stones.

'''Mulch''' is an item used during the [[Struggling sapling (Forestry event)|Struggling sapling]] [[Forestry#Forestry events|Forestry event]], where players must create the right combination of resource piles to feed the [[struggling sapling]]. These resource piles include [[droppings]], [[green leaves]], [[rotting leaves]], [[splintered bark]], and [[wild mushrooms]].

Players can use the mulch's "check" option to see which ingredients are currently used in it. In addition, the "History" option shows players an interface of the [[struggling sapling]]'s health, as well as the best and most recent combination of mulch discovered during the event. As it cannot be deposited into a [[bank]], it is recommended that players bring it to the Ancient Vault immediately, as the [[Mysterious Figure]] may appear and attack the player if they have it in their inventory for too long.

As it cannot be deposited into a [[bank]], it is recommended that players bring it to the Ancient Vault immediately, as the [[Mysterious Figure]] may appear and attack the player if they have it in their inventory for too long.

If you lose the medallion during the quest, you can recover it by returning to where you fought [[The Whisperer]]. The entrails will be there and you can grab another medallion without having to fight again.

A '''coin pouch''' is an item obtained from [[pickpocketing]] certain [[NPC]]s, which contains several [[coins]] depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the [[Ardougne Diary]], where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via [[Thieving training#Levels 45-55/91: Blackjacking|blackjacking]] yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If [[rogue equipment]] is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

cases.name: Moonlight grub
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Moonlight grub detail.png|150px|left]]
'''Moonlight grubs''' are items collected from [[grubby sapling]]s found within the Earthbound and Streambound Caverns in [[Neypotzli]]. During [[Perilous Moons]], players must collect one and use a [[pestle and mortar]] on it to obtain [[moonlight grub paste]].

When leaving Neypotzli, this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: {{Mes|The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.}}

This item is used as the icon for [[moonlight potion]]s on the in-game Herblore [[skill guide]], despite the uncrushed grubs not being a reagent for the potion.

cases.name: Moonlight grub paste
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Moonlight grub paste detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Moonlight grub paste''' is made by using a [[pestle and mortar]] on [[moonlight grub]]s, which are picked from [[grubby sapling]]s within [[Neypotzli]]. Players can sometimes receive multiple paste from one grub, depending on their [[Herblore]] level.

Moonlight grub paste can be combined with a [[vial of water]] to create [[moonlight potion]]s, which can be used as a potion whilst fighting the [[Moons of Peril]] to provide melee skill boosts and prayer restoration. Players may create an extra dose of potion, with the chance depending on the player's Herblore level.

Additionally, one moonlight grub paste is requested by [[Eyatlalli]] during [[Perilous Moons]].

When leaving Neypotzli this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: {{Mes|The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.}}

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Jug of blessed sunfire wine detail.png|130px|left]]
A '''jug of blessed sunfire wine''' is an item created by blessing a [[jug of sunfire wine]] at the [[exposed altar]] found south of [[the Teomat]], which is made by using two [[sunfire splinters]] on a [[jug of wine]] with a pestle and mortar in your inventory. Sunfire splinters '''cannot''' be added to a [[jug of blessed wine]]; it must be added to an unblessed jug first. It is used in the process of sacrificing [[blessed bone shards]] at the [[libation bowl]], where one jug can sacrifice 400 shards. Players will also need 2 [[Prayer points]] per sacrifice.

When used at the libation bowl, in place of a regular jug of blessed wine, the [[Prayer]] experience gained per blessed bone shard is increased from 5 to 6, equivalent to an increase of 200 Prayer experience per sunfire splinter used for a total of 2400 experience per jug.

When buying the sunfire splinters on the [[Grand Exchange]], this results in a cost of {{Coins|2*{{GEP|Sunfire splinters}}/400}} gp per Prayer experience.

Be aware that the jug of blessed sunfire wine '''cannot''' be stored in the bank.

cases.name: Jug of blessed wine
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Jug of blessed wine detail.png|130px|left]]
A '''jug of blessed wine''' is an item created by blessing a [[jug of wine]] at the [[exposed altar]] found south of [[the Teomat]], requiring level 30 in [[Prayer]]. It is used in the process of sacrificing [[blessed bone shards]] at the [[libation bowl]], where one jug can sacrifice 400 shards; players will also need 2 [[Prayer points]] for each sacrifice.

Alternatively, players may use a [[jug of blessed sunfire wine]] instead, which gives each bone shard 6 Prayer experience instead of 5. This requires having added two [[sunfire splinters]] to an unblessed jug of wine; sunfire splinters '''cannot''' be added to a jug of blessed wine.

The jug of blessed wine cannot be stored in the bank.

cases.name: Bandages
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Bandages (The Heart of Darkness) detail.png|left|width=100x100]]
'''Bandages''' are used to heal the player and [[Prince Itzla Arkan]] during the second trial in the quest, [[The Heart of Darkness]]. The latter is particularly important as the prince cannot take any of the player's food. They heal 18 hitpoints when to Prince Itzla and less{{clarify|Seen 12 HP from one source, need to confirm it does not scale}} when used on the player.

There are three [[medical box]]es in the room, each containing five bandages. The boxes will be refilled if the player fails the trial. Any bandages remaining will be removed from the player's inventory upon proceeding to the next trial.

cases.name: Digweed
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Digweed detail.png|150px|left]]
'''Digweed''' can be harvested from [[Digweed (plant)|digweed plants]] within the [[Mastering Mixology]] [[minigame]]. Using digweed with any potion in the minigame will double the amount of resin and [[Herblore]] experience gained when placing it on the conveyor belt. 

Digweed can be obtained by picking the herb once it has matured, which happens periodically after depositing finished potions on the conveyor belt. The player will receive a notification in game chat indicating which corner of the lab has the matured plant. If not picked within 33 ticks (19.8 seconds), a mature digweed will die.

A potion can only be improved with digweed once; attempting to use multiple digweeds on the same potion returns the message {{mes|This potion has already been improved with digweed.}}

Having any digweed in the inventory will prevent another digweed from spawning until used or destroyed, though using the [[drop trick]], or mixing the digweed into an unfinished potion, allows the player to gather multiple digweeds. 

'''Note:''' Leaving the lab will cause any digweed in the player's inventory to wither away, meaning they cannot be banked or stockpiled. When this happens, a game message appears stating {{mes|Your digweed withers away as you leave the lab.}} However dropping the digweed while inside the minigame,  leaving via teleport, and then telegrabbing it will allow you leave with the digweed.

Digweed cannot be banked; attempting to do so gives you this message {{mes|A magical force prevents you from banking this item!}}. However, potions that have been improved with digweed '''can''' be banked. 

{{Bug|Using a potion with a digweed (instead of a digweed with a potion) comes up with a chat message stating that you mixed the potion into the potion to improve its quality. (e.g {{Mes|You mix the mammoth-might mix into the Mammoth-might mix, drastically improving its quality!}})}}

When opened, the player will receive a [[rotten tomato]] or [[smelly sock]].

cases.name: Polycatalytic guardian stone
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Polycatalytic guardian stone detail.png|120px|left]]
'''Polycatalytic guardian stones''' are items used to power-up [[the Great Guardian]] during a game of [[Guardians of the Rift]], alongside [[Elemental guardian stone|elemental]], [[Polyelemental guardian stone|polyelemental]], and [[Catalytic guardian stone|catalytic]] guardian stones.

They are obtained by crafting [[Combination rune|combination runes]] when imbuing [[guardian essence]] at a [[Runic altar#Catalytic|catalytic runic altar]], accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 [[Runecraft]] experience and 3 catalytic energy (instead of the normal 2) per polycatalytic guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Currently, only [[Aether rune|Aether runes]] give Polycatalytic Energy.

{{Guardians of the Rift}}

A '''coin purse''' is an item obtained during [[The Final Dawn]], on a table in the middle floor in [[Forebearer Janus]]' house. Opening the purse will give five [[coins]], resulting in an empty pouch, which is then used on a plant pot filled with sand to create a sandy coin purse; the sandy purse is finally used on a [[Branch (The Final Dawn)|branch]] to create a [[makeshift blackjack]].

Players can use either the filled or empty coin pouch on [[Captain Vibia]]; however, she will say that there is no use for it.

A '''coin purse''' is an item obtained during [[The Final Dawn]], on a table in the middle floor in [[Forebearer Janus]]' house. Opening the purse will give five [[coins]], resulting in an empty pouch, which is then used on a plant pot filled with sand to create a sandy coin purse; the sandy purse is finally used on a [[Branch (The Final Dawn)|branch]] to create a [[makeshift blackjack]].

Players can use either the filled or empty coin pouch on [[Captain Vibia]]; however, she will say that there is no use for it.

Ancient teleporter
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Ancient teleporter detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Ancient teleporters''' are items that can be found by searching the chest right next to the [[Lift Platform (Crypt of Tonali)|lift platform]] between the [[Crypt of Tonali]] and the [[Ruins of Mokhaiotl]] after completion of [[The Final Dawn]].

The two teleporters can be placed anywhere in the area, even between floors, as long as they are placed within 30 tiles of each other. Once a pair has been placed, the [[Tonali Teleporter]]s can be used to transport players to the other instantly. Should players wish to relocate the teleporters, they may simply pick one up and right-click "Recall" to obtain the other.

The teleporters are useful in speeding up travel to [[Ruins of Mokhaiotl]] by placing one teleporter on the tile where players arrive via lift platform, and another further north. It can also be used for quicker access to specific areas of the cavern; for example, to the central area where multiple [[earthen nagua]] and [[moonlight moth]]s are found together.

cases.name: Antique lamp
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Antique lamp (salvaging) detail.png|130px|left]]
An '''antique lamp''' is rewarded from handing in a [[Kudos#Salvaging_relics|relic]] obtained while sorting [[salvage]] to [[Curator Haig Halen]]. A lamp is only given for the first hand-in of a specific relic, with subsequent hand-ins rewarding 5,000 coins instead.

Rubbing the lamp grants 5,000, 10,000, or 15,000 in any skill at or above level 30, 40, or 50 respectively. The amount given varies depending on the relic handed in, with relics with higher [[Sailing]] requirements offering larger lamps:
* 5,000 experience — [[rusty locket]], [[mouldy block]], [[dull knife]]
* 10,000 experience — [[broken compass]], [[rusty coin]], [[broken sextant]]
* 15,000 experience — [[smashed mirror]], [[mouldy doll]]

The lamps '''cannot''' be banked, but the relics handed in to receive the lamps can be banked.

A '''coin pouch''' is an item obtained from [[pickpocketing]] certain [[NPC]]s, which contains several [[coins]] depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the [[Ardougne Diary]], where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via [[Thieving training#Levels 45-55/91: Blackjacking|blackjacking]] yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If [[rogue equipment]] is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

cases.name: Serving platter
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Serving platter detail.png|130px|left]]'''Serving platter''' is an item used in the [[2025 Christmas event]]. During the event, the player can place drinks on the platter, including [[beer]], [[dwarven stout]], [[cider]], [[wine]], milk, chocolate milk, and [[eggnog]]. The player can also place food from crates in the basement of the [[Blue Moon Inn]]. The main courses include chicken, beef, jubbly, nut roast, mushroom wellington, and trout. Side dishes include potatoes, sprouts, cauliflower, broccoli, cabbage, peas, parsnips, carrots, and stuffing.

cases.name: Scribbled notes
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Scribbled notes detail.png|130px|left]]
The '''Scribbled notes''' can be obtained from the [[note on a table]] during the [[2026 Easter event]], or reclaimed from the [[Easter Bunny]] if lost.

Reading the notes shows different hints to help the player find Archibald depending on their progress through the event:

*"I heard there is a potion that can make me stronger!" - Search shelves in [[Apothecary]]'s pharmacy.
*"I heard about a guy who sells bendy sticks." - Search stepladder on the 2nd floor of [[Lowe's Archery Emporium]]. You will also receive an [[egg box]], for which the code to unlock it is "LOWE".
*"I heard the view from up here is the best!" - Search the wall at the very top of the [[Varrock church]]. You will go through a cut-scene.
*"I heard you can buy shiny, pointy sticks from this guy." - Search the table with weapons on it at [[Varrock Swordshop]].
*"I heard about an evil place of worship. Sounds cool!" - Go to the building in south-east [[Varrock]], where the [[Mage of Zamorak]] resides and search the chair.
*"Bil noun omen." - Anagram for [[Blue Moon Inn]]. Search the bed in the easternmost room on the top floor to find a decoy egg box. Click the egg box to receive the next note.
*"I heard there is a real king, in a court!" - Go to [[Varrock Palace]] and search the eastern suit of armour in [[King Roald]]'s room.
*"I heard there is this massive vault of riches underground." - Go to [[Varrock west bank]] and catch [[Archibald]] underground,  next to the gate.

Return the egg to the [[Easter Bunny]] to complete the event.

{{2026 Easter event}}

cases.name: Egg box
cases.sourceContext: [[File:Egg box detail.png|130px|left]] '''Egg box''' is an item found upon searching the [[Stepladder (2026 Easter event)|stepladder]] upstairs in [[Lowe's Archery Emporium]] during the [[2026 Easter event]]. The box can be opened using the code LOWE, which updates the [[scribbled notes]] with a new clue. [[File:Egg box interface.png|left|thumb|The interface seen when unlocking the egg box.]] The rotation of each dial is randomised each time the egg box is opened. The four dials can each be configured to one of ten letters: # R N K S O A D L E T # E C L I R O P A N T # L A T D M F P B W S # N A L I R E S O T U This results in 10,000 possible letter combinations. A second version of the egg box is found when searching the [[Bed (2026 Easter event)|bed]] in the [[Blue Moon Inn]]. This version is a decoy egg, and provides updated scribbled notes immediately upon opening. {{2026 Easter event}}

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Poem scroll detail.png|left|100px]]
The '''poem scroll''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] during the escape from the [[Castle Drakan]] of [[Vampyrium]], found on a table in the dining hall. The text of the poem provides the times required for solving the [[Grandfather clock (The Blood Moon Rises)|grandfather clock]] puzzle. The hands are set to the directions (North, West) and number of kills (eleven, four) mentioned.

The solution is derived from reading the map and using the locations as shown on the map (Apsul on the right and Virer on the left) to tell you where to input the answers in the poem. It starts in Apsul as mentioned on the first line, so you start on the right (East) clock and change the big hand for the father and the small hand for the son. The first answer is North "The father then went north,", so you input 12 to point it North and use the big hand as it's the father, then the next is four "For he vanquished four prey." so you input 4 and use the small hand as it was the son who vanquished four. It then goes on to say that they met again in Virer, so you move to the left (West) clock and continue. The next answer is eleven "The father killed eleven," so you input 11 on the big hand for it was the father and finally the last answer is west "Then departed to the West." so you input 9 to point it West on the small hand as it was the son who departed.

cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Daeyalt ore (The Blood Moon Rises) detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Daeyalt ore''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] during the escape from the [[Castle Drakan]] of [[Vampyrium]], found on the [[shelves (Castle Drakan laboratory)|shelves]] in the laboratory on the top floor.

They are combined with other ingredients using the [[Refiner (The Blood Moon Rises)|refiner]] to make [[chemical vial]]s.

{{The Blood Moon Rises}}

cases.name: Chemical vial
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Chemical vial detail.png|100px|left]]
'''Chemical vials''' are an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] during the escape from the [[Castle Drakan]] of [[Vampyrium]].

They are made by combining [[Vial of water (The Blood Moon Rises)|vials of water]], [[Vial of blood (The Blood Moon Rises)|vials of blood]], [[Daeyalt ore (The Blood Moon Rises)|Daeyalt ore]], and [[Pure essence (The Blood Moon Rises)|pure essence]] in the [[Refiner (The Blood Moon Rises)|refiner]] in the laboratory on the top floor.

{{The Blood Moon Rises}}

cases.name: Old cog
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Old cog detail.png|130px|left]]
The '''old cog''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] in [[Sangvesti]]. It is used to fix the old drawbridge leading to the [[Sotfa Forest]].

If the player dies with this item in the inventory, it will be dropped in the same place where they died.

cases.name: Jovkai key
Loop half of key
cases.sourceTitle: Loop half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Loop half of key (The Blood Moon Rises) detail.png|left|100px]]
A '''loop half of key''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] in [[Sangvesti]]. Found in the house east of the blacksmith's building, it is combined with the [[Tooth half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)|tooth half of key]] to create the [[Myrmel key]].

cases.name: Tooth half of key
cases.sourceTitle: Tooth half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Tooth half of key (The Blood Moon Rises) detail.png|left|100px]]
A '''tooth half of key''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] in [[Sangvesti]]. Found in the house east of the [[Altar (Sangvesti)|altar]], it is combined with the [[Loop half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)|loop half of key]] to create the [[Myrmel key]].

cases.name: Myrmel key
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Myrmel key detail.png|130px|left]]
The '''Myrmel key''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] in [[Sangvesti]]. Made by combining the [[Loop half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)|loop half]] and [[Tooth half of key (The Blood Moon Rises)|tooth half of key]], it is used to open the Myrmel doors within the village.

Vitur key
Trapdoor key
Bolt cutters
Crank wheel
Dusty book
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dusty book detail.png|130px|left]]
A '''dusty book''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] in [[Sangvesti]], found in a bookshelf in the house north of the prayer altar. Reading the book reveals that it contains the [[Vitur key]].

cases.name: Spine
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Spine detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Spines''' are a thrown weapon obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] through the [[Sotfa Forest]], where fifty can be found on the ground upon arriving at the nylocas nest.

The spines are mainly used to attack [[Nylocas Toxobolos]], allowing players to kill them without having to leave [[Vampyrium]]. Should additional spines be needed, the nearby [[dead venator]] can be harvested for fifty spines.

Despite the spine's high ranged strength, there is no reason to collect more than needed, as they will disappear as soon as players leave the area.

cases.name: Dead blood serpent
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dead blood serpent detail.png|150px|left]]
'''Dead blood serpents''' are obtained upon successfully wrangling a [[blood serpent]]. Three can be combined to create a [[serpent rope]].

cases.name: Serpent rope
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Serpent rope detail.png|left|150px]]
A '''serpent rope''' is an item obtained during [[The Blood Moon Rises]] whilst attempting to escape from [[Lowerniel Drakan]] through the [[Sotfa Forest]], where three [[dead blood serpent]]s are needed to create one.

It can be attached to a [[Long branched tree (The Blood Moon Rises)|long branched tree]] in the same area to cross the river.

cases.name: Tick
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Tick (item) detail.png|left|130px]]
'''Ticks''' are found while the player is fleeing through the forests of [[Vampyrium]] during [[The Blood Moon Rises]]. When chopping down [[darkwood tree]]s, wrangling [[blood serpent]]s, swinging with the [[serpent rope]], or withdrawing supplies from the shelter remains, there is a chance that a tick will be added to the player's inventory, indicated by the message {{mes|colour=red|You feel something crawl into your inventory...}} 

Carrying a tick in the inventory will slowly deal 1 hitpoint of damage until removed by left-clicking on it; the damage will not be increased if multiple ticks are present.

Upon leaving the area with the [[blood serpent]]s, all ticks in the player's inventory are removed.

cases.name: Amitire leaves
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Amitire leaves detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Amitire leaves''' are obtained from [[amitire plant]]s during the quest [[The Blood Moon Rises]]. They are used to make [[amitire stew]] to help [[Safalaan Hallow]] recover.

cases.name: Amitire stew
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Amitire stew detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Amitire stew''' is made from [[stew]] and [[amitire leaves]] during the quest [[The Blood Moon Rises]]. It is given to [[Safalaan Hallow]] to help him recover.

cases.name: Hallowed marks
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Hallowed marks (The Blood Moon Rises) detail.png|left|100px]]
'''Hallowed marks''' are given to the player by [[Efaritay Hallow]] during the quest [[The Blood Moon Rises]]. They are combined with the [[blisterwood flail]] and a [[blisterwood sickle (e)]] at an anvil to create the [[hallowed flail]].

The [[Hallowed mark|Hallowed marks]] obtained from the [[Hallowed Sepulchre]] cannot be used in their stead, only the quest variant can be used.

cases.name: Healing potion
Silvthrill ballista
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Silvthrill ballista detail.png|130px|left]]
The '''silvthrill ballista''' is a special two-handed [[crossbow (weapon)|crossbow]] used during the quest [[The Blood Moon Rises]], when [[Lowerniel Drakan]] begins his assault on [[Sugadinti]]'s hideout in [[Vampyrium]].

The player uses it to destroy the various portals Drakan summons. It can only fire [[silvthrill javelin]]s, which are also given to the player during this segment of the quest. No experience (ranged or otherwise) is rewarded with use of the ballista. Both the silvthrill ballista and silvthrill javelins are removed from the player's inventory upon completion of the segment.

cases.name: Silvthrill javelin
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Silvthrill javelin detail.png|110px|left]]
The '''silvthrill javelin''' is a special type of [[ranged]] ammunition used by the [[silvthrill ballista]]. The silvthrill javelins and ballista only appear during the quest [[The Blood Moon Rises]], when [[Lowerniel Drakan]] begins his assault on the hideout in [[Vampyrium]]. Both the silvthrill ballista and silvthrill javelins are removed from the player's inventory upon completion of the segment.

Letvek in a bucket
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Letvek in a bucket detail.png|130px|left]]
A '''letvek in a bucket''' can appear in the player's inventory while collecting sap from the [[engorged bloodwood tree]] (it does '''not''' replace the sap that would have been gained). It can be gently shooed away by clicking the bucket; until this is done, the player can no longer chop the tree.

Despite the chatbox message warning that players should get rid of the [[letvek]] in the bucket before it drinks their sap, the letvek will not drink any [[bucket of bloodwood sap]] that is present in the inventory; however, players can use one on the letvek in the bucket to feed it, satiating its hunger and sending it scurrying away.

cases.name: Wooden spikes
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Wooden spikes detail.png|130px|left]]
'''Wooden spikes''' are used in [[goat hunting]] in southern [[Wyrmscraig]]. Players are required to line a [[Goat Pit|pit]] with spikes before luring the [[Wyrmscraig Goat|goats]] into them. They can be obtained from the [[spikes supply]] found near [[Geoff]] the farmer.

cases.name: Large hat
Worn journal
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Worn journal detail.png|130px|left]]
The '''worn journal''' is found on a [[table]] in the basement of [[Ardeaglais]]. It cannot be picked up by the player, nor does [[Telekinetic Grab]] work on it, but it can be investigated to read it.

cases.name: Scrawled notebook
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Scrawled notebook detail.png|130px|left]]
The '''scrawled notebook''', title '''scrawled notes''', is found by inspecting the [[sunstone monolith]] during [[Fallen From Grace]]. It was written by [[Keenan]], documenting his research into the monolith.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a [[bookcase]] within a [[player-owned house]] or the searchable [[Rocks (Scrawled notebook)|rocks]] next to the [[sunstone monolith]].

cases.name: Ancient sunstone core
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Ancient sunstone core detail.png|130px|left]]
An '''ancient sunstone core''' is obtained from a locked chest in the basement of [[Ardeaglais]] during the [[Fallen From Grace]] quest. The core is broken open by destroying it, or using a [[hammer]] or [[chisel]] on it, to obtain the [[staircase key]].

cases.name: Staircase key
Dull sunstone core
cases.sourceContext:
[[File:Dull sunstone core detail.png|130px|left]]
A '''dull sunstone core''' is an item obtained during [[Fallen From Grace]], upon switching it with a [[sunstone core]] on the [[broken golem]] found in the [[Wyrmscraig Cavern]].
